title: High-dimensional Mean-Field Games by Particle-based Flow Matching
abstract:
Mean-field games (MFGs) study the Nash equilibrium of systems with a continuum of interacting agents, which can be formulated as the fixed-point of optimal control problems. They provide a unified framework for a variety of applications, including optimal transport (OT) and generative models. Despite their broad applicability, solving high-dimensional MFGs remains a significant challenge due to fundamental computational and analytical obstacles. 

In this work, we propose a particle-based deep Flow-Matching (FM) method to tackle high-dimensional deterministic MFG computation.
In each iteration of our proximal best response scheme, particles are updated using first-order information, and a flow neural network is trained to match the velocity of the sample trajectories in a simulation-free manner. 
Theoretically, in the optimal control setting, we prove that our scheme converges to a stationary point sublinearly, and upgrade to linear (exponential) convergence under additional convexity assumptions.
Our proof uses FM to induce an Eulerian coordinate (density-based) from a Lagrangian one (particle-based), and this also leads to certain equivalence results between the two formulations for MFGs when the Eulerian solution is sufficiently regular.
Our method demonstrates promising performance on non-potential MFGs and high-dimensional OT problems cast as MFGs through a relaxed terminal-cost formulation.
problem: Solving high-dimensional mean-field games remains computationally and analytically challenging despite broad applicability to optimal transport and generative models.
approach: Proposes particle-based Flow-Matching method using proximal best-response scheme where particles update via first-order information and flow network trained to match sample trajectory velocities.
contribution: Proves convergence to stationary point sublinearly with linear convergence under convexity, demonstrates performance on non-potential MFGs and high-dimensional optimal transport problems.
